name: Aurochs
intro: Zib! Central Europe, 50 BCE, deep in an ancient forest. Something enormous is crashing through the trees: a wild bull taller than Glorp's ship!
description: The aurochs was a huge wild ox, the ancestor of every cow alive today. Bulls stood up to about 1.8 metres at the shoulder, were black with a pale stripe down the back, and had long, forward-curving horns; cows were smaller and reddish-brown. Aurochs roamed forests, river valleys and grassland across Europe, Asia and North Africa. Around 10,000 years ago people began taming them, and over thousands of years they became domestic cattle. Julius Caesar described wild aurochs in the forests of Germania as being "a little below the elephant in size". As forests were cleared for farms and the animals were hunted, they slowly vanished. The very last aurochs, a cow, died in Jaktorów Forest in Poland in 1627.

facts.height: ~1.5–1.8 m at the shoulder (bulls bigger than cows)
facts.extinct_year: 1627 (the last one, a cow, in Jaktorów Forest, Poland)
facts.cause: Hunting, forests cleared for farms, and diseases caught from farm cattle

habitat.biome: Temperate forest, river valleys and wet grassland

terrain.value: Open forest with clearings, river meadows and marshes
terrain.why: It grazed in clearings and wet meadows and sheltered in the forest.

temperature.why: European winters bring frost and snow; summers are warm but not hot.

humidity.why: It liked damp river valleys and marshy meadows full of lush grass.

oxygen.why: Ordinary air, like the cattle it gave rise to.

pressure.why: It lived mostly in lowland river valleys, close to sea-level air pressure.

hotspots.label: Forest clearing
hotspots.fact: Aurochs grazed sunny clearings and wet meadows, then slipped back into the forest for shelter.

hotspots.label: Frosty leaves
hotspots.fact: Winters here bring frost and snow; summers are warm but never hot.

hotspots.label: Marshy meadow
hotspots.fact: Damp river meadows grow the lushest grass, and aurochs loved them.

hotspots.label: River valley
hotspots.fact: This lowland river valley isn't far above sea level, so the air pressure is just like at the coast.

hotspots.label: Huge horns
hotspots.fact: A bull's horns curved forwards and could be up to about 80 cm long. Every cow alive today is descended from aurochs.

hotspots.label: Giant hoofprints
hotspots.fact: Hoofprints bigger than Glorp's hand. Bulls were black with a pale stripe down the back; cows were reddish-brown.

hotspots.label: Roman scroll
hotspots.fact: Julius Caesar wrote that these wild oxen were "a little below the elephant in size". The last one died in Poland in 1627.
